decision.summary: The Federal Reserve kept its target for the federal funds rate unchanged at 1 3/4 percent.

changes.quote: The information that has become available since the last meeting of the Committee confirms that economic activity is continuing to increase.
changes.explanation: The Fed acknowledges that the economy is still growing.

changes.quote: However, both the upward impetus from the swing in inventory investment and the growth in final demand appear to have moderated.
changes.explanation: The boost from businesses restocking items and general demand have both slowed down.

changes.quote: The Committee expects the rate of increase of final demand to pick up over coming quarters, supported in part by robust underlying growth in productivity, but the degree of the strengthening remains uncertain.
changes.explanation: Strong worker productivity should help demand pick back up later, but officials remain unsure how strong that rebound will be.

tone_quotes.quote: The Federal Open Market Committee decided today to keep its target for the federal funds rate unchanged at 1 3/4 percent.

In these circumstances, although the stance of monetary policy is currently accommodative, the Committee believes that, for the foreseeable future, against the background of its long run goals of price stability and sustainable economic growth and of the information currently available, the risks are balanced with respect to the prospects for both goals.

for_you.text: Card rates should not move on this decision; a $5,000 balance at about 13.62% APR costs about $56.75 a month in interest.

Mortgages track the 10-year Treasury, not the fed funds rate. The 10-year was 4.75% and moved -13 bp on the day; if that move passed through, the payment on a new $300,000 30-year loan at 6.71% would fall by about $25.81 a month.
Savings yields should stay roughly where they are, since the Fed held rates.
Unemployment was 5.8%, and employers added an average of -35k jobs a month over the prior 3 months.

for_country.text: CPI inflation was 1.2% over the past year (May 2002); core PCE inflation, the Fed's preferred gauge, was 1.7%, against a 2% goal.
Real GDP grew at a 3.4% annualized pace in the latest reported quarter.
The 2-year Treasury yield, the most Fed-sensitive market rate, moved -15 bp on the day.

card.whats_next: The statement signals that the Federal Reserve plans to keep rates steady while evaluating whether economic growth will strengthen as expected. Officials believe the risks to their long-run goals are currently balanced.
